#### The dashboard, traced — stack and heap at every step

**What is being answered.** How a correct-looking dashboard publishes a wrong number — line by line, with the real times.

Three functions and nothing clever: `onEvent` buckets by `minOf(e.et)` (the right clock), `publishDue` declares a minute done when `watermarkAfter(i)` passes its end, and `onLate` is the three policies.

Watch `closed` across steps 1 and 3. It is `false` while the minute is still open and `true` when id 7 finally lands — and that single boolean is the whole design problem. Everything before it is correct, and the answer is still 8 against a truth of 12.

The animation steps through the code, holding each line long enough to read the STACK (call frames and their locals) and the HEAP (allocated arrays and objects) as they are AT THAT MOMENT. Expand any step to study it on its own.

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch01-system-memory/ch01-system-memory.svg" alt="The dashboard, traced — stack and heap at every step, 4 steps showing stack and heap" width="980">

<details>
<summary><b>Step 1 of 4</b> — the 12:00 minute accumulates the events that have arrived</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch01-system-memory/frames/step-01.svg" alt="Step 1: the 12:00 minute accumulates the events that have arrived" width="980">

After events 0 and 1, `display[0]` holds 5 + 3 = 8. `closed` is false — the minute has not been published, so nothing is a revision yet. Everything here is correct; the problem is not in this function.

</details>
<details>
<summary><b>Step 2 of 4</b> — the watermark passes 12:01, so the minute is PUBLISHED</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch01-system-memory/frames/step-02.svg" alt="Step 2: the watermark passes 12:01, so the minute is PUBLISHED" width="980">

At event 3 (id 3, seen 12:02:12) the watermark reaches 70, which is ≥ 0 + 60. So minute 0 joins `published` and ops sees **8**. The true answer is 12. The pipeline is not behind — it has decided.

</details>
<details>
<summary><b>Step 3 of 4</b> — id 7 arrives 148s later, into a minute already published</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch01-system-memory/frames/step-03.svg" alt="Step 3: id 7 arrives 148s later, into a minute already published" width="980">

`minute` is 0 — correct, it is bucketed by event time — and `closed` is now **true**, because 0 is in `published`. This is the exact line where a pipeline discovers it has already lied. For 148s, from 12:02:12 to 12:04:40, the screen said 8 and the answer was 12.

</details>
<details>
<summary><b>Step 4 of 4</b> — three policies, three different published histories</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch01-system-memory/frames/step-04.svg" alt="Step 4: three policies, three different published histories" width="980">

`"drop"` returns immediately: `display[0]` stays 8, permanently 33% low. `"revise"` re-enters `onEvent`, so `display[0]` becomes 12 and `revisions` becomes 1 — a published number moved, and every downstream reader must cope. The third option, waiting 230s, never reaches this function because nothing was published early enough to need fixing.

</details>
